data.cultural_impact: The name Mayer has been adopted and used extensively in Jewish communities, particularly among the Ashkenazi Jewish population. In Germanic origins, it is derived from the Middle High German word ‘meier’ which translates to steward, mayor, or farmer. Thus, over time, the name Mayer also came to signify someone in positions of authority, like a leader, mayor, or ruler. Given its ancient background, the name has been associated with affluence, intelligence, and power. Mayers are regarded as individuals of high social status, bearing responsibilities towards their families and communities.
